hypotheses.justification: This follows from the other hypotheses. B is finite over R, so the Mathlib instance `Module.Finite.base_change` (Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Finite.lean) makes A ⊗[R] B finite over A. For each i, the A-linear map (LinearMap.proj i).comp e.toLinearMap : A ⊗[R] B → S i is surjective: any y comes from e.symm (Pi.single i y), using classical DecidableEq. So `Module.Finite.of_surjective` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean) gives Module.Finite A (S i). Add `haveI : ∀ i, Module.Finite A (S i) := fun i => Module.Finite.of_surjective _ (surj i)` at the start of the proof. The rest of the proof (the rewrites with gapsw7_x3x_trace_baseChange, Algebra.trace_eq_of_algEquiv and gapsw7_x3x_trace_pi) then runs unchanged. Neither the statement nor any other binder mentions this instance. It is deletable on its own, together with [Module.Finite R B] it is not claimed.

This follows from the other hypotheses. If A is a trivial ring (Subsingleton), both sides of the equation lie in A and are equal. Otherwise A is nontrivial. Each S i is free and finite over A and ι is a Fintype, so ∀ i, S i is finite over A (Module.Finite.pi), and through e so is A ⊗[R] B (Module.Finite.equiv). A ⊗[R] B also has the base-changed basis (Algebra.TensorProduct.basis) indexed by Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R B. The lemma `Module.Finite.finite_basis` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Cardinality.lean: [Nontrivial R] [Module.Finite R M] (b : Basis ι R M) : Finite ι) shows that this index type is finite. Then `Module.Finite.of_basis` applied to Module.Free.chooseBasis R B gives Module.Finite R B, and the original proof applies. This is deletable on its own, with [∀ i, Module.Finite A (S i)] still present; it is not claimed that both can be deleted together.
